analysis.title: High core CPI for a third month in a row
key_insights: October core CPI rose 0.3% m/m, above the 0.2% consensus, the second consecutive monthly upside surprise per the report (the report's header says third month in a row for core CPI coming in higher than expected).
The upside surprise was small but broad-based. Core services ex rents rose 0.4% and rents rose 0.29%, both 0.1-0.15pp above SEB's forecast.
Core goods were 0.1pp below expectations only because of lower used car prices. Other goods rose 0.4% m/m, 0.1-0.5pp above expectations.
The 3-month annualized core CPI change is approaching 4% and sits at the high end of the recent range. SEB says this will concern some Fed members who focus on that measure.
Core CPI y/y is 2.8% versus 2.6% previously, but October y/y figures are SEB estimates because no October 2025 indices exist (government shutdown).
Energy prices rose 0.7%, slightly less than expected and slower than the prior two months. Food rose 0.4% m/m, above expectations, after three muted months.
Tourist services, a main driver of inflation in the last two months, kept rising at a more modest pace.
SEB raised its near-term inflation forecast slightly. Higher energy prices delayed the headline slowdown and raised the risk of indirect effects such as higher transportation costs.
Market-based Zillow rents suggest rents could start rising faster again, possibly from weaker home purchase affordability and higher mortgage rates pushing demand toward rentals.
Wage inflation continues to slow, which SEB says implies any inflation upturn will be temporary. SEB still expects core CPI and core PCE back at target by end of 2028.
If sustained, the recent sharp decline in oil prices will pressure headline inflation lower and, with a lag, ease some upward pressure on core CPI.

tension_points.bull_case: Wage inflation continues to slow, so any inflation upturn will be temporary. SEB expects core CPI and core PCE back at target by end of 2028 as tariff, energy and AI build-out impulses fade.
tension_points.bear_case: Core CPI has surprised higher three months in a row, the 3-month annualized rate is approaching 4%, and goods, rents and services are showing upward pressure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained fall in oil prices would ease headline and, with a lag, core pressure. Further rent acceleration or goods price increases would weaken the temporary-upturn view.
